ButtonHelp.Content = ?  How to read these numbers
ButtonHelp.ToolTip = Opens a page that explains every number on this screen. Read it the first time, and whenever a number does not look as you expected.
TextBlockStatusLine.Text = showing: family clustering only · no quantitation loaded
TextBlockStatusLine.ToolTip = What the share column currently shows: its denominator, how shared peptides were treated, and how many families got a value. It changes only when you press Recalculate.
Label.ToolTip = Filters the table by locus, description or domain. Separate several terms with commas; a row is shown when it has ANY of them.

TextBoxSearch.ToolTip = Type part of a locus, description or domain. Separate several terms with commas, for example: metalloprotease, SVMP; a row is shown when it has ANY of them. Filtering never changes a percentage.
Label.ToolTip = How many protein families there are: visible after the filters, and in the whole file.
LabelNumberOfGroups.ToolTip = Left: families among the rows shown. Right: families in the whole file. They differ while a filter, such as Hide Reverse, is on.
Label.ToolTip = The sequence-identity threshold USearch used to build these families.
LabelClusterThreshold.ToolTip = The USearch identity threshold this file was built at. Higher gives more, smaller families. To change it, run USearch again and generate a new .fcf.
Label.ToolTip = Whether these families were merged further by their description words, and at what threshold.
LabelWordSimilarity.ToolTip = How the families were built: 'none' means by sequence identity only, a number is the threshold of the last Recluster by Words, and 'keywords' means a keyword merge.

ButtonAlignSelected.ToolTip = Aligns the selected proteins and opens the alignment in a new window, to check that a family's members really are homologous. Disabled until at least two rows are selected in the Data Browser tab.

ButtonFetchDomains.ToolTip = Asks UniProt for each protein's Pfam domains, which needs the internet once. They fill the Domains column, the Search box finds them, the super cluster preview can choose by them, and saving keeps them in the file. Family numbers do not change.
Label.ToolTip = How alike two families' descriptions must be before they are merged into one.

DecimalUpDownWordReCluster.ToolTip = Families whose description words score at or above this value are merged (0.10 to 1.00). Default 0.95 merges only near-identical wording; lower it towards 0.90 to gather related families.
Label.ToolTip = Words to ignore when comparing descriptions.

TextBoxWordsToBeExcluded.ToolTip = Words to ignore when comparing descriptions, separated by commas or spaces, for example: protein, domain, fragment. Use it when a common word pulls unrelated families together; it also applies to Create Super Cluster.
ButtonWordCluster.ToolTip = Merges families whose descriptions are at least as similar as the Similarity value. Family numbers change and percentages are recalculated; press Undo to step it back.
Label.ToolTip = Keywords that define one deliberately large family.

TextBoxSuperClusterWording.ToolTip = Keywords separated by commas or spaces, for example: metalloproteinase, SVMP; the proteins of matching families are listed, and the ones you keep become one family. Words in quotes are a phrase that must appear together in that order: "ribosomal subunit", "ribosomal protein" with 'match any word' gathers either.
Label.ToolTip = Whether one protein's description must contain ALL the keywords or just ANY one of them for its family to be offered.

ComboBoxSuperClusterMatch.ToolTip = 'match all words' offers a family only if one of its descriptions has every keyword; 'match any word' offers it if one has at least one keyword. A single keyword works the same either way. Default: match all words.
SuperMatchAll.ToolTip = A family is offered only if one of its descriptions contains EVERY keyword.
SuperMatchAny.ToolTip = A family is offered if one of its descriptions contains AT LEAST ONE of the keywords.
Label.ToolTip = Words that keep a protein OUT of the super cluster even when its family matches.

TextBoxSuperClusterExclude.ToolTip = Whole words that keep a protein out of the super cluster, separated by commas or spaces, for example: inhibitor, matrix. The rest of its family still joins. Use it to gather 'phospholipase' while leaving out 'phospholipase inhibitor'.

ButtonSuperCluster.ToolTip = Shows every protein that would join, each with a tick, before anything changes, then gathers the ticked ones into one family, and Undo steps it back. Disabled until you type a keyword in the box to the left.
Label.ToolTip = Changes every row you have selected in the table at once, instead of one row at a time.
Label.ToolTip = The family number to give every selected row.

TextBoxBatchUserId.ToolTip = A family number for every selected row; leave it empty to keep their numbers. An existing number joins that family, an unused one makes a new family. The family they join, and any family they leave that still has members, is locked against reclustering.
Label.ToolTip = The text to write into the User Annotation column of every selected row.

TextBoxBatchAnnotation.ToolTip = Text for the User Annotation column of every selected row, for example: cellular proteins. Leave it empty to keep their annotations; annotations are exported with the CSV.
ButtonApplyToSelected.ToolTip = Gives every selected row the User ID and/or annotation typed to the left. Select with Ctrl+click or Shift+click, or Ctrl+A for all visible rows; Undo steps it back.
TextBlockBatchStatus.ToolTip = What the last 'Apply to selected rows' did, or why it did nothing.
Label.ToolTip = How many families are protected from automatic reclustering. A locked family is never merged by Recluster by Words or Create Super Cluster.
LabelLockCount.ToolTip = The number of locked families in this file, including numbers a later merge took out of use. It shows what the next reclustering will refuse to merge.

ButtonManageLocks.ToolTip = Opens the list of locked families, where you can read and remove locks. A removal reaches the disk only when you save the Family Cluster File. Disabled while no family is locked.
ButtonUndo.ToolTip = Undoes the last curation change, such as a merge, a User ID edit or a lock removal, up to 50 steps in this session. Disabled until there is a change to undo.
ButtonLoadQuantData.ToolTip = Loads a PatternLab project (.plp) to fill the share column for these families. It must be exported at PEPTIDE level; a protein-level export makes every row read 0.
TextBlock.ToolTip = Which quantitation project is loaded, if any.
TextBlockPLPStatus.ToolTip = The name of the loaded PatternLab project. Until one is loaded, the share column stays empty.
Label.ToolTip = What to do with a peptide that belongs to more than one family.
Label.ToolTip = What the numbers in the share column are a percentage OF.
Label.ToolTip = What the Full XIC share column is a percentage OF.

ComboBoxFullXicBasis.ToolTip = What the Full XIC share column is divided by. Use 'the quantified signal' for a composition (a pie chart of the families), 'the total ion current' for each family's share of the whole sample. Applies at once.
FullXicBasisQuantified.ToolTip = Divides by every quantified peptide, each counted once.
FullXicBasisTic.Content = the total ion current of all runs
FullXicBasisTic.ToolTip = Divides by the summed TIC of every run the computation recorded.
TextBlockFullXicSummary.ToolTip = What the Full XIC column adds up to: the families, the peptides shared between families, and the peptides with no family.
TextBlockFullXicSummary.Text = No full XIC computed for this project yet: run File · Compute / update full XIC to fill the Full XIC share column.
TextBlockQuantProfile.ToolTip = What the loaded project says about its own quantitation: the divisor it used, and which reporting modes it can therefore support.
TextBlockQuantProfile.Text = Load a project in Layer 2 to see how it was exported.

ButtonRecalculateQuantitation.ToolTip = Applies the two choices on the left to the share column; the button changes colour when the table is out of date. Disabled until a PatternLab project is loaded in Layer 2.
Run.Text = • Two sources: the Full XIC column comes from Compute / update full XIC; Layer 2 is optional, for a PatternLab .plp (the 'Share of signal' column)
Run.Text = • Shared peptides applies to both columns; Report XIC as and Recalculate apply to the .plp column, Full XIC share of to the Full XIC column
Run.Text = • The two lists answer different questions, and the status line at the top always says which one is on screen
CheckBoxShowXICOnly.ToolTip = Hides families with no quantitation, so only the families your project measured are shown. Percentages do not change. Off by default.

CheckBoxExcludeContaminants.ToolTip = Hides entries whose identifier contains 'contaminant' (keratins, trypsin, serum proteins) from the table and the CSV. Percentages do not change, so in '% of identified signal' the visible ones no longer add up to 100%.

CheckBoxExcludeReverse.ToolTip = Hides decoys, whose identifier starts with 'Reverse_', from the table and the CSV. Nothing is deleted and no percentage moves; keep them visible while judging the clustering.

ButtonSaveReport.ToolTip = Writes the visible rows, with the table's columns, to a CSV file; shares are fractions from 0 to 1 with a dot as decimal point. Disabled while every row is hidden by a filter.

ButtonExportComposition.ToolTip = Writes the Full XIC family composition to a CSV: one row per family, plus the unattributed peptides and, with 'Family-unique only', the shared ones. Disabled until the project has a full XIC (File · Compute / update full XIC).

TextBlock.Text = Re-extract every identified peptide, and any kept de novo precursor, straight from the RAW acquisitions with the full isotope envelope, and store the numbers in this project. Nothing derived is computed here: the shares and the family rollups are a later step. Runs are matched to acquisitions by file name.
Label.ToolTip = The folder with the .raw files of these runs. Runs are matched to files by name, so the order of the files does not matter.
TextBoxRawDirectory.ToolTip = Type or paste the folder with the .raw files here, or use Browse. Runs are matched to files by name.
ButtonBrowseRaw.ToolTip = Choose the folder with the .raw files. The chosen folder is written into the box beside this button.
Label.ToolTip = The SEPro result file (.sepr2) with the identified peptides of these runs. Choose the one made from the same runs as the RAW files.
TextBoxSeproPackage.ToolTip = Type or paste the path of the .sepr2 file here, or use Browse. It must come from the same runs as the RAW files.
ButtonBrowseSepro.ToolTip = Choose the SEPro identification file (.sepr2). The identified peptides are taken from this file.
Label.ToolTip = The folder with your PEAKS and/or DeepNovo exports. Only the source chosen below is read and filtered. Leave it empty to quantify only the identified peptides.
TextBoxDeNovoDirectory.ToolTip = Type or paste the de novo export folder here, or use Browse. Subfolders are searched too. Leave it empty to store only the identified peptides.
ButtonBrowseDeNovo.ToolTip = Choose the de novo export folder. Its subfolders are searched for the source chosen below. Leave the box empty to store only the identified peptides.
Label.ToolTip = Which de novo export to read. PEAKS ALC and DeepNovo SCORE are different scales, so each keeps its own cutoff and they are never mixed.

ComboBoxDeNovoSource.ToolTip = The de novo source to read, or a union of PEAKS and DeepNovo. In a union, a precursor called by both is measured once under the PEAKS call, and the DeepNovo call is kept beside it.
ComboBoxItem.Content = Union: PEAKS de novo only + DeepNovo
ComboBoxItem.Content = Union: PEAKS de novo all + DeepNovo
Label.ToolTip = The minimum PEAKS ALC (average local confidence) a call needs to be kept. Used only when a PEAKS source is selected.
TextBoxPeaksMinimumAlc.ToolTip = PEAKS ALC cutoff, 0 to 100, default 80. It applies only to PEAKS calls.
Label.ToolTip = The minimum DeepNovo SCORE a call needs to be kept. Used only for DeepNovo; a SCORE of 80 is not the same as a PEAKS ALC of 80.
TextBoxDeepNovoMinimumScore.ToolTip = DeepNovo SCORE cutoff, 0 to 100, default 80. It applies only to DeepNovo calls.
Label.ToolTip = How many isotopes each peptide can be credited, counting M+0 as the first. It is a maximum: an isotope that is not found adds nothing. Leave it at 6.
IntegerUpDownIsotopes.ToolTip = Isotope ceiling, 1 to 6, default 6. Use 6 for the full envelope; 1 counts only the monoisotopic peak, as PatternLab's stored quants do.
Label.ToolTip = How many points a peak needs before it is quantified. The program counts one padding point on each side, so 3 means at least one real detection and 5 means at least three. Default 3.

IntegerUpDownMinPoints.ToolTip = Minimum points per peak, 1 to 20, default 3 (one real detection). Use 5 to require three real detections; 1 switches the check off. The value is saved with the project.
TextBlockBasis.ToolTip = The settings the next computation will use: isotope ceiling, minimum points, extraction window and MS1 tolerance. The last two are fixed to match the stored quants.

ButtonCompute.ToolTip = Measures every identified peptide, and any kept de novo precursor, from the RAW files and stores the numbers in this project. Needs at least the RAW folder and the .sepr2 file; Save the project afterwards to keep them.

ButtonViewSpectrumComparison.ToolTip = Opens a read-only table with one row per file, scan and precursor, comparing the PEAKS, DeepNovo and PatternLab calls, and can save it as CSV. Disabled until a computation finishes.
TextBlockSpectrumComparisonPath.Text = The spectrum comparison CSV is written after a successful computation.
TextBlockSpectrumComparisonPath.ToolTip = Where the latest computation saved the spectrum comparison CSV. It holds the same rows as the table.
TextBlockStatus.ToolTip = Shows what the computation is doing and what it found: progress, per-run counts and any refusal.
ButtonClose.ToolTip = Close this window. A finished computation is kept in the project; Save the project to write it to disk.

Label.ToolTip = The folder holding the de novo export. Its sub-folders are searched too, for the files of the source chosen below.

TextBlockNativeConfidence.ToolTip = The confidence score that is read and filtered. PEAKS ALC and DeepNovo SCORE are different scales and are not interchangeable.
Label.ToolTip = Shortest de novo sequence kept, in residues. Short sequences match proteins by chance, so lower it only with a reason. Default 7.
TextBoxMinLength.ToolTip = A whole number from 1 to 100. A value out of range is refused when you press Load and filter, and the previous value stays.
LabelMinimumSourceConfidence.ToolTip = Lowest overall confidence kept (PEAKS ALC or DeepNovo SCORE). The two scales are not equivalent, and neither is a calibrated FDR. Default 80%.
TextBoxMinAlc.ToolTip = A number from 0 to 100, decimals allowed. Spectra scoring below it are dropped. A value out of range is refused when you press Load and filter.
Label.ToolTip = How many consecutive residues must each reach the stretch floor. This keeps a sequence with one clearly read region and drops a uniformly mediocre one. Default 5.
TextBoxStretchLength.ToolTip = A whole number from 1 to 100; a longer stretch is stricter. A value out of range is refused when you press Load and filter.
Label.ToolTip = The confidence every residue in the stretch must reach; a lower residue breaks the run. Keep it high. Default 90%.
TextBoxStretchFloor.ToolTip = A number from 0 to 100, rounded to a whole number. A value out of range is refused when you press Load and filter.
ButtonLoadAndFilter.ToolTip = Reads every export file of the chosen source in the folder and keeps the rows that pass the length, confidence and stretch filters.
LabelFilesFound.ToolTip = Export files of the chosen source found in the folder and its sub-folders. Zero means the wrong folder or the wrong source.
LabelRowsRead.ToolTip = De novo rows read from the files, before filtering. Truncated lines are skipped.
LabelRowsKept.ToolTip = Rows that passed all three filters, and their share of the rows read. Every later step works from these rows.
TextBlockPerRunBreakdown.Text = No import yet. The breakdown per run appears here.
TextBlockPerRunBreakdown.ToolTip = Rows read and kept for each run. Runs are named by file name, not by order. A run keeping far fewer rows than the others is worth checking.
Label.ToolTip = The PatternLab search result (.sepr2) to compare the de novo rows with. It must be the search of the same runs, or every row will look new.
TextBoxSeproPackage.ToolTip = Type or paste the .sepr2 file's full path. It is only read when you press Reconcile.
ButtonBrowseSeproPackage.ToolTip = Pick the .sepr2 file. Nothing is read until you press Reconcile.
ButtonReconcile.ToolTip = Joins the kept de novo rows to PatternLab by file name and scan. Sequences are compared only when the charge matches and the precursor m/z is within 20 ppm.
LabelVerdictDeNovoOnly.ToolTip = Kept de novo spectra with no PatternLab identification in the same run and scan. This is the new evidence the later steps work on.
LabelVerdictCoIsolated.ToolTip = PatternLab identified this scan, but not at the same charge and precursor m/z (within 20 ppm). This may be co-isolation; it is not a sequence disagreement.
LabelVerdictRedundant.ToolTip = Same scan, precursor and sequence as a PatternLab identification, so it adds nothing new. None at all usually means the search is not of the same runs.
LabelVerdictWeakPsm.ToolTip = Same sequence as PatternLab, but the PatternLab XCorr is below the threshold. Kept for review, not counted as new signal.
LabelVerdictConflict.ToolTip = Same scan, charge and precursor m/z (within 20 ppm), but a different sequence. Kept for review and left out of the de novo quantitation.
LabelReviewQueueCount.ToolTip = Rows kept for review: alternative sequences plus matches whose PatternLab XCorr is below the threshold.
LabelOverlapScan.ToolTip = Spectra both programs reported in the same file and scan. This does not yet mean the same precursor, since one scan can hold several.
LabelOverlapPrecursor.ToolTip = Same file, scan and charge, with precursor m/z within 20 ppm. Sequences are compared only inside this group.
LabelOverlapExact.Content = Same scan + charge, exact sequence: -
LabelOverlapExact.ToolTip = Same file, scan and charge, and the same sequence as the best PatternLab match once modifications are removed. I and L count as different here.
LabelOverlapDivergent.Content = Same scan + charge, alternative sequence: -
LabelOverlapDivergent.ToolTip = Same file, scan and charge, but a different sequence once modifications are removed. The stricter m/z-matched count is shown separately.
ButtonExportSummary.ToolTip = Saves a small CSV with the counts above for each run. Disabled until a reconciliation has been run.
ButtonExportReviewQueue.ToolTip = Saves the review queue as a CSV, with both sequences and every matching field, for checking by hand.
ButtonExportOverlapStudy.ToolTip = Saves the full overlap study as a CSV: same-scan matches and differences, then the split by precursor. Each row states its definition.

DataGridReviewQueue.ToolTip = Rows with a comparable precursor but a different sequence, plus matches with a low PatternLab XCorr. They are left out of the de novo quantitation and listed here for review.
ExpanderStandalone.ToolTip = Advanced: extract areas, attribute to families and partition ion current without a project. If you have a .fqproj, use steps 3 and 4 on the Home instead.
TextBlock.Text = Standalone run (advanced): extract, attribute, partition without a project

TextBlock.Text = These are the SAME computations the main Compute full XIC and Analytics screens now run. They are kept here only for a de-novo-only run that has no .fqproj project: with a project, use steps 3 and 4 on the home instead, which store and read the result.
TextBlock.ToolTip = Why this section is optional: with a .fqproj project, steps 3 and 4 on the Home do the same work and store the result.
Label.ToolTip = The folder holding the .raw files of these runs. Each run's RAW is found by file name. It defaults to the export folder's parent.
TextBoxRawDirectory.ToolTip = Type or paste the RAW folder's full path. The list below shows which runs found their file. Nothing is read until you press Extract.
ButtonBrowseRawDirectory.ToolTip = Pick the RAW folder. The list below updates at once; nothing is read until you press Extract.

ButtonExtractXic.ToolTip = Measures the M+0 peak area of each kept de novo precursor from the RAW files, one run at a time. Disabled until Step 2 has been reconciled and every kept run has found its RAW.
TextBlockRawMatchPreview.Text = No reconciliation yet. Which kept run found which .raw appears here.
TextBlockRawMatchPreview.ToolTip = For each kept run, the .raw found for it or the missing file name. Runs are matched by file name, and Extract stays disabled while any is missing.
LabelXicRunsExtracted.ToolTip = Runs extracted so far, out of the kept runs. Partition ion current stays blocked until every kept run is extracted.
LabelXicTotalM0.ToolTip = The de novo M+0 ion current, summed over distinct peaks, so a peak sampled by several MS2 scans counts once.
LabelXicElapsed.ToolTip = How long the extraction took, in seconds. A repeat over the same runs is much faster, from the cache.
DataGridXicStats.ToolTip = One line per run. The first counts are per MS2 scan; Distinct peaks and the areas are per chromatographic peak, so a peak sampled by several scans counts once.
Label.ToolTip = The .fcf whose proteins the de novo peptides are searched against, and whose User IDs give the families. Filled in if a family file was already open.
TextBoxHomologyFcf.ToolTip = Type or paste the .fcf file's full path. It is only read when you press Search.
ButtonBrowseHomologyFcf.ToolTip = Pick the .fcf file. Nothing is read until you press Search.

ButtonSearchHomology.ToolTip = Aligns each distinct kept peptide to the family file's proteins and assigns the hits to families. It does not need extracted areas. Disabled until Step 1 has kept at least one row.
Label.ToolTip = Fraction of a peptide that must match a protein exactly before it is scored. Default 0.80; lower values let in chance matches, so watch the decoy-only count.
TextBoxMinIdentity.ToolTip = A number from 0 to 1, with a dot as the decimal separator. A value out of range is refused when you press Search.
Label.ToolTip = How many proteins one peptide may be assigned to, best scores first. Default 3. Raising it spreads shared peptides over more families.
TextBoxTopHits.ToolTip = A whole number, 1 or more. A value below 1 is refused when you press Search.
CheckBoxConsiderILSame.Content = I and L are one residue
CheckBoxConsiderILSame.ToolTip = Treat isoleucine and leucine as the same residue when matching, since they have identical mass. On by default; leave it on.
CheckBoxKQEquivalent.Content = K and Q are one residue
CheckBoxKQEquivalent.ToolTip = Treat lysine and glutamine as the same residue when matching (they differ by 0.036 Da). Off by default; turning it on widens every family.
Label.ToolTip = Text that marks a decoy protein in the family file. If it is wrong, decoys count as targets and the mapped count looks better than it is.
TextBoxDecoyLabel.ToolTip = The decoy prefix, case-sensitive. Default Reverse_, which FamilyQuant writes. An empty box is refused when you press Search.
LabelHomologyPeptides.ToolTip = Distinct peptide sequences searched. A sequence read in many spectra is searched once, so this is below the kept row count.
LabelHomologyMapped.ToolTip = Peptides assigned to at least one target protein, and their share of those searched. Read it next to the decoy-only count.
LabelHomologyDecoyOnly.ToolTip = Peptides that matched only decoy proteins: the false-match control. If it is close to the mapped count, the identity threshold is too low.
LabelHomologyUnmatched.ToolTip = Peptides that matched no protein at this identity. In venom de novo data this is common, and it is not an error.
LabelHomologyElapsed.ToolTip = How long the search took, in seconds, so an unusually slow search can be noticed.
ButtonExportHomologyCsv.ToolTip = Saves one line per peptide with its families, proteins and whether it is ambiguous. Disabled until a search has been run.
DataGridHomologyFamilies.ToolTip = One line per family reached, most peptides first, target hits only. A peptide in two families counts in both, so the column does not sum to the peptides searched.
Label.ToolTip = The PatternLab project giving the identified segment of each bar. If it cannot give per-run values (merged replicates), the .xic2 below is used.
TextBoxPartitionPlp.ToolTip = Type or paste the .plp file's full path. It is only opened when you press Build partition.
ButtonBrowsePartitionPlp.ToolTip = Pick the .plp file. Nothing is read until you press Build partition.
Label.ToolTip = Optional fall-back holding each run's quants separately, used only when the .plp cannot give per-run values. Give it if you have it.
TextBoxPartitionXic2.ToolTip = Type or paste the .xic2 file's full path, or leave it empty. It is opened, read only, when you press Build partition.
ButtonBrowsePartitionXic2.ToolTip = Pick the .xic2 file. Nothing is read until you press Build partition.

DataGridPartition.ToolTip = One line per run plus one for all runs. The three shares always add up to 100%. A negative remainder is a real finding and is never set to zero.
ButtonSavePartitionCsv.ToolTip = Saves every number behind the chart, per run and for all runs together. Disabled until a partition has been built.
ButtonOpenPartitionWindow.ToolTip = Opens the chart in its own window, with its own save button. Disabled until a partition has been built.

"HOW THE FAMILIES ARE BUILT: TWO STAGES"
"Clustering runs in two stages. The fast first pass groups the database quickly,"
"but it is greedy and order-sensitive: two proteins that align above your identity"
"can still land in separate families, because the second was only ever compared"
"against the seed of a family it did not quite match. That leaves biological holes,"
"The \"Exhaustive clustering\" checkbox (on by default) closes them. After the first"
"pass it aligns EVERY pair of proteins in full and merges two families whenever the"
"proteins reach your identity over most of the LONGER sequence. Proteins that share"
"only a short motif fail that coverage test and are correctly kept apart, so an"
"angiotensin fragment does not pull in a whole metalloproteinase, but two full-length"
"metalloproteinases the fast pass split are put back together."
"This is single linkage: every pair at or above the identity chains its two families"
"into one, so the merge can chain a whole superfamily together. That is the intended"
"meaning of the threshold, not a side effect: the identity you choose IS the tightness"
"knob. Raise it for more, smaller families; lower it to chain more together."
"The exhaustive pass runs at any database size and is never capped. On a database"
"over 10,000 sequences the all-versus-all alignment takes longer and more memory, so"
"you are warned once before it starts and can proceed or stop; it still runs at any"
"size if you proceed. Turn the checkbox off to use the faster first-pass-only"
"clustering, which is quicker but leaves the holes."

"De novo only        nothing in the search shares that spectrum. This is new"

"The different-precursor-context verdict is worth understanding. A mass spectrometer"
"isolates a window, not a molecule, so two species eluting together are"
"fragmented into ONE spectrum: a chimeric spectrum. PatternLab explained one of"
"them; the de novo call may be an alternative ion in that window. The scan number"
"alone cannot establish duplication, sequence conflict, or biological truth."

"THE REVIEW QUEUE, AND WHY IT IS MANUAL"
"The queue holds exactly two of the five verdicts: overlapping alternatives, and"
"agreements where PatternLab's own evidence was weak. The other three are"
"results, and a result does not need a decision."
"An overlapping alternative is a de novo hypothesis on a comparable precursor."
"answer decides which is right: a cross-correlation and "
"same scale, are not calibrated against each other, and are not measuring the"
"same thing. An automatic rule here would be an invented threshold dressed as a"
"result, and it would be invisible afterwards."
"So the program presents the evidence and decides nothing. The table is"
"read-only and shows both sequences side by side with the cross-correlation on"
" plus the weakest residue confidence on the de"
"novo side, plus how far apart the two precursors were in ppm. It is a"
"review set for the loaded source. Export it and"
"the evidence can be inspected away from this screen. These rows are not added to"
"the de novo signal while unresolved, so review cannot inflate quantification."
"An equal-but-weak row is retained in the review export rather than labelled as an"
"ordinary redundant confirmation. It is excluded from additive de novo quantification"
"until reviewed, so the evidence remains visible without double-counting its signal."
"Layer 3 opens each run's .raw once and integrates a chromatogram for every kept"
"precursor, at its own anchor scan. The acquisitions are found BY FILE NAME, one"
"run is held in memory at a time, and the results are cached beside the RAW"
"files so a second session over the same runs costs seconds instead of minutes."
"M+0 is the monoisotopic peak alone: the isotope that carries no heavy carbon."
"The whole isotope envelope (M+0 plus M+1 plus M+2) is measured beside it, but"
"only as a diagnostic, and it is deliberately kept out of the chart in Layer 5."
"PatternLab's stored quants are M+0, and one bar cannot be built from two"
"different bases without saying something false about the comparison."
"The counts come in TWO GRAINS and the column headings say which:"
"    ANCHORS   one request per MS2 scan that fired on that precursor. \"Rows"
"              in\", \"unique precursors\" and \"with signal\" are anchors."
"    PEAKS     one integrated elution peak. \"Distinct peaks\" and every area"
"They differ because one elution peak is usually sampled by several MS2 scans:"
"several anchors, one peak, and the extractor hands that same peak back to each"
"of them. Every total on this screen is summed over DISTINCT PEAKS. Summing per"
"anchor instead would add the same trapezoid once per MS2 event, which inflates"
"the ion current by a few percent, always upwards, and never fails a check. The"
"\"redundant anchors\" and \"redundant area\" columns report exactly what that"
"The \"shared-window bound\" column is a BOUND, not a correction. Two peaks of the"
"same precursor inside one extraction window can be two genuine elution events"
"across a long gradient, or one broad peak entered twice; telling them apart"
"needs each peak's scan span, which this extraction does not record. So they are"
"all kept, and the most that could still be double-counted (each window's total"
"less its largest peak) is printed instead of being quietly removed."
"A de novo sequence has no protein attached to it. Layer 4 asks whether it looks"
"like one anyway: each DISTINCT kept sequence is aligned against the proteins of"
"a Family Cluster File, and every surviving hit is attributed to the User ID"
"family of the protein it landed in. One file answers both halves, which is why"
"a hit can never land in a protein the family table does not know."
"The sequences are deduplicated first: the same tag read in fifty spectra is one"
"alignment, not fifty, so \"peptides searched\" is far below the rows kept in"
"Layer 1. The minimum identity is a PREFILTER, not the score: a protein that"
"never reaches that fraction of literal identity is never aligned at all."
"Isoleucine and leucine are treated as one residue there by default, because"
"they have the same mass and a fragment spectrum cannot tell them apart, so"
"punishing the engine's arbitrary choice between them would be punishing physics."

"family file carries reversed sequences beside the real ones. A peptide that"
"found only reversed proteins was attributed to something that does not exist,"

"on its own: if the two are of the same size, the threshold is too low, whatever"
"It is not an FDR because nothing here is calibrated into a corrected error rate"
"per hit: there is no competition between a target and its decoy for one"
"spectrum, and no q-value is computed or implied. It is one number to read the"
"other against. A peptide that found both keeps its targets and drops its"
"decoys; a peptide that found only decoys keeps them, which is the entire point"
"of having them, and it stays out of the family table below."
"Most kept sequences match nothing at all, and that is not a defect. They are"
"the reason a de novo search was run."

"current, read from the RAW with no trimming at either end, and it is cut into"
"    PatternLab   the ion current of the peptides the database search"
"    De novo      what the kept de novo set adds on top of that."
"    Remainder    what is left, and still has no owner."

"thing that had to be earned instead is COMPARABILITY: both of the first two"

"The word alone is not enough, so the source is printed with it: \"recorded\""

TextBlock.ToolTip = Why the automatic answer is a lower bound, not a recommendation. Help · How to read these numbers explains more.

TextBlock.Text = The target/decoy score only detects a target aligning to a decoy, which marks where alignment becomes noise. It cannot see two unrelated target families being fused, so use it as a floor - not as a budget.
